summary: Moves RFC 3525, Gateway Control Protocol Version 1, to Historic status and obsoletes it. It is an informational memo.

eli5.summary: This is a note that says an older phone-gateway control specification is now retired and should not be used for new work.

subtitle: RFC 3525, the Megaco gateway control protocol, is retired to Historic because the ITU-T kept developing it as H.248.1.

tldr.problem: RFC 3525 describes the Megaco/H.248 Gateway Control Protocol Version 1, but the ITU-T has since taken ownership and moved on to newer versions.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5125 reclassifies RFC 3525 as Historic and obsoletes it.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3525 may still serve as an introduction to the protocol, but is misleading as a description of it as currently standardized or deployed.

today: RFC 5125 is an Informational memo that obsoletes RFC 3525 by reclassifying it as Historic. The protocol itself continues as ITU-T Recommendation H.248.1.

sections.title: Where the Protocol Came From
sections.content:
The protocol in RFC 3525, Gateway Control Protocol Version 1, was developed jointly by the IETF Megaco Working Group and ITU-T Study Group 16. The ITU-T published it as Recommendation H.248.1 (originally H.248) with the same contents as the RFC.

Since that initial development the ITU-T has taken ownership of the protocol and has continued to work on it.
sections.eli5: Two groups built it together. Then one of them took it home and kept improving it.

sections.title: Why It Is Historic
sections.content:
The original protocol underwent corrections and clarifications. H.248.1 version 1 was republished in March 2002 with all agreed changes up to then, and later corrections are collected in an Implementors' Guide. Version 2 was published in May 2002 and is described as the version most widely deployed at present, and the one other standards bodies such as 3GPP use as the basis for their own profiles. Version 3 followed in September 2005.

The memo concludes that RFC 3525 may serve as an introduction to the Megaco/H.248 protocol, but it is misleading as a description of the protocol as currently standardized or deployed. Reclassifying it to Historic is appropriate under RFC 2026.
sections.eli5: The old edition of the book is fine for a first look, but the newer editions say different things now. So the old one is shelved as history.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content: The document needs no new IANA actions. The IANA registries established by RFC 3525 and extended by later versions of ITU-T H.248.1 remain in force, along with the requirement for expert review by an IESG-designated expert. The memo also says that reclassifying RFC 3525 has no security implications.
sections.eli5: The lists of official names and numbers stay exactly as they were, so nothing else changes.

references.text: Groves, C., Ed., Pantaleo, M., Ed., Anderson, T., Ed., and T. Taylor, Ed., "Gateway Control Protocol Version 1", RFC 3525, June 2003.
